title: Jira → DevRev migration POC
summary: Parallel-run DevRev environment seeded for a Jira customer. Jira projects map to DevRev products, components/epics become capabilities, and story/bug/task issue types become features. Auto-detects Jira CSV exports (Issue key, Summary, Issue Type headers).

ui_guidance_sections.title: Prerequisites — verify before running setup steps
steps: Confirm the DevRev user behind your PAT has the Admin role. Builder/Member roles cannot reach all Settings menus, and several integrations require Admin to install snap-ins.
Confirm the PAT itself was generated by that same Admin user. PATs inherit the creator's role at the moment they were issued — escalating the user later does NOT re-scope existing tokens.
If a step below returns an 'access required' or HTTP 403 error, regenerate the PAT from an Admin account and rerun `dia doctor` before retrying.
Some Settings menus are scoped per-workspace; confirm you're operating in the workspace the customer will use, not your default DevRev org.

ui_guidance_sections.title: Map Jira priorities to DevRev
steps: Jira Highest/Blocker → DevRev priority p0 (priority_v2: 1)
Jira High → p1 (priority_v2: 2)
Jira Medium → p2 (priority_v2: 3)
Jira Low/Lowest → p3 (priority_v2: 4)
Note: Jira uses 5-level priorities; DevRev uses 4. Merge Highest+Blocker → p0 and Low+Lowest → p3.

ui_guidance_sections.title: Map Jira issue types to DevRev work types
steps: Jira Bug → DevRev issue (use the 'bug' tag to preserve the type distinction)
Jira Story → DevRev issue (use the 'story' tag)
Jira Task → DevRev issue (use the 'task' tag)
Jira Epic → DevRev capability or feature (epics become parts in the hierarchy, not work items)
Jira Sub-task → DevRev issue linked to its parent via 'is_dependent_on'
If you need tickets instead of issues for customer-facing items, use type 'ticket' in the CSV column_map.

ui_guidance_sections.title: Map Jira project structure to DevRev parts
steps: Each Jira Project becomes a DevRev product (top-level part).
Jira Components become DevRev capabilities under that product.
Jira Epics become DevRev features (or capabilities if they're large initiatives).
Jira Fix Versions → use DevRev sprints or custom fields to track release targets.
Adjust the parts hierarchy in this blueprint to mirror your actual Jira project structure before applying.

ui_guidance_sections.title: Map Jira workflow to DevRev stages
steps: This blueprint creates custom stages that complement DevRev's built-in pipeline: Ready for Dev, Code Review, and QA Validation. Combined with the built-in stages (backlog, in_development, completed), these mirror a typical Jira Kanban workflow.
After applying, go to Settings → Object Customization → Stage Diagrams to set allowed transitions.
If your Jira workflow has additional statuses (e.g., 'Waiting for QA', 'Blocked'), add them as custom_stages in this blueprint before applying.
Map Jira workflow transitions to DevRev stage diagram transitions for parity.

ui_guidance_sections.title: Importing your real Jira export
steps: Export issues from Jira: Issues → Search → Export → CSV (All fields or Current fields).
Drop the CSV next to this blueprint and add a `csv` entry: `{ "path": "./jira-issues.csv", "entity": "issues" }`.
The agent auto-detects Jira headers (Issue key, Summary, Issue Type, Assignee, Reporter, Priority, Status) and applies the column map automatically.
Override mappings via `column_map` if your Jira instance uses custom fields.
For large exports (>1000 issues), split into multiple CSVs by project to keep apply runs manageable.

ui_guidance_sections.title: Bidirectional Jira sync (parallel-run period)
steps: Settings → Integrations → Snap-ins → Install the Jira Airsync snap-in.
Authenticate with your Jira Cloud instance (API token + email).
Map Jira Projects → DevRev Products (use the parts hierarchy seeded above as the target).
Map Jira issue types → DevRev work types (issues for engineering items, tickets for support).
Enable bidirectional sync for the parallel-run period.
After cutover: disable sync, import the final delta CSV, then archive the Jira project.

ui_guidance_sections.title: Configure Jira integration
steps: Settings → Integrations → Jira
Provide your Atlassian Cloud URL and an API token from id.atlassian.com.
Map DevRev parts → Jira projects (one-to-one is simplest for a POV).
Choose which DevRev work types sync to Jira issues (typically issues, not tickets).
Enable bidirectional status/comment sync.
